doc.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Working with Woody Allen
summary: Hyman says Allen knows music, picks tunes and leaves details to him.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah. He kind of had all his eggs in one basket you know, so musical but a little short on the social skills and all that.
What’s Woody Allen like to collaborate with?

Well if I had to characterize it in a particular way I’d say knowledgeable, musically. He knows music. He picks the tunes. He’s open to suggestion and it’s easy to work with him, as opposed to some people who don’t know very much about the subject at all and may still give you a hard time. But the people who know that they don’t know about the subject, they’re okay to work with, they leave it to you. Woody is both. Woody leaves it to me and to the other people, I presume, the costumers and the set designers and so forth, but he has certain specific ideas and in the case of music he knows quite a bit on his own, so we’ve always gotten along pretty well.
